                    ### Question
                    Over the course of a year, 5 children with identical congenital heart defects were referred to a pediatric cardiac surgeon for evaluation. All 5 children had stable vital signs and were on appropriate medication. Upon review of medical records, all of them had a loud holosystolic murmur over the third intercostal space at the left sternal border. The surgeon ordered echocardiograms for all 5 children and recommended surgical closure of the defect in one of them. Which of the following patients required surgical repair of their defect?

                    ### Options
                    opa. A 4-month-old male infant with a 12-mm muscular defect, without heart failure, pulmonary hypertension or growth failure
opb. An 11-month-old female infant with a 6-mm membranous defect, without heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or growth failure
opc. A 2-year-old boy with a 2-mm supracristal defect, without heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or growth failure
opd. A 5-year-old girl with a 2-mm membranous defect, no heart failure, a Qp:Qs ratio less than 2:1, and no growth failure
ope. A 7-year-old boy with an 11-mm muscular defect and severe pulmonary vascular disease non-responsive to pulmonary vasodilators

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient who requires surgical repair of their congenital heart defect is option e, a 7-year-old boy with an 11-mm muscular defect and severe pulmonary vascular disease non-responsive to pulmonary vasodilators. The presence of severe pulmonary vascular disease that is unresponsive to treatment indicates the need for surgical intervention despite the absence of heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or growth failure.
